newsitem.title: UK: ISDA issues contract continuity provision for EMU.
newsitem.headline: ISDA issues contract continuity provision for EMU.

text.p: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said a provision issued on Wednesday would enable counterparties to agree that a European single currency does not affect the continuity of contracts.
Developed by ISDA's EMU documentation taskforce, the economic and monetary union (EMU) continuity provision was designed to protect parties to a swaps transaction from circumstances created by EMU.

"The provision states that such events as the introduction of a single European currency or disappearance of price sources will give neither party a unilateral right to walk away from or modify the terms of transactions governed by their master agreement," ISDA said in a statement.
It followed a European Union regulation on certain provisions relating to the euro launch and proposed legislation for contract continuity recently introduced in New York, Illinois and California.

"The intention is that inclusion of this provision will not be inconsistent with these legislative developments and will provide guidance on the matters covered within the 'four corners' of the parties' written contract," said Matthew Elderfield, ISDA's London-based European policy director.
He said EMU taskforces dealing with documentation and market practice continued to examine issues linked to a single European currency.
